title: Height from homogeneous independence at a rational point
statement: Let $k$ be a field and $A$ a Noetherian commutative $k$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring, def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient]. Let $\varepsilon:A\to k$ be a $k$-algebra homomorphism and put $I=\ker\varepsilon$. Let $\iota$ be a finite index set and choose $x_i\in I$ for $i\in\iota$. Suppose (i) every $a\in I$ can be written $a\equiv\sum_i c_i x_i\pmod{I^2}$ with $c_i\in k$, and (ii) for every integer $r\ge0$ and every homogeneous polynomial $f\in k[X_i:i\in\iota]$ of total degree $r$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring], $f(x)\in I^{r+1}$ implies $f=0$. Then $\operatorname{ht}(I)=\#\iota$, where height is the supremum of lengths of chains of primes contained in $I$ [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring].

proof.text: Put I=ker ε. Since ε(algebraMap(c))=c, A/I is k. Induct on r using the spanning congruence and the product definition of I^r to represent every element of I^r/I^(r+1) by a homogeneous polynomial of degree r. The independence assumption makes these maps injective. They respect multiplication, giving gr_I A ≃ k[X_i].

source.place: Proof, Dimension paragraph: the local dimension equals the cotangent dimension; polynomial associated graded criterion

proof.text: Localize at I. Each I^r/I^(r+1) is annihilated by I, so every element outside I acts by the nonzero scalar ε(s); localization preserves the graded pieces. The local ring R=A_I is Noetherian, with polynomial associated graded ring and residue field k. Its dimension is the height of I.

source.place: Proof, Dimension paragraph: the local dimension equals the cotangent dimension; polynomial associated graded criterion

proof.text: Nakayama shows that the chosen lifts generate the maximal ideal m of R. Krull intersection shows that R is m-adically separated: apply the localization intersection lemma at m; its element f outside m is a unit, so the intersection itself is zero. When the index set is empty, Nakayama gives m=0, hence R is a field of dimension zero.

source.place: Proof, Dimension paragraph: the local dimension equals the cotangent dimension; polynomial associated graded criterion

proof.text: For a nonempty index set choose x_1. A nonzero y has finite m-adic order. Its initial form times X_1 is nonzero in the polynomial graded ring, so x_1 y has order ord(y)+1. Thus x_1 is a nonzerodivisor, and (x_1)∩m^r=x_1 m^(r-1) for r≥1. The kernel in each degree of gr R→gr(R/(x_1)) is therefore the degree-r part of (X_1). Thus the quotient has polynomial graded ring on one fewer variable.

source.place: Proof, Dimension paragraph: the local dimension equals the cotangent dimension; polynomial associated graded criterion

proof.text: Induct on the number of variables, using the preceding strictness for each successive quotient. The dimension of R/(x_1) is n-1. A nonzerodivisor in the maximal ideal of a Noetherian local ring drops dimension by exactly one, hence dim R=n. Substituting dim R=ht I proves the assertion, including n=0.

If lifts of a basis of the cotangent space have no homogeneous relations in the associated graded ring of a maximal ideal, its height equals the cardinality of the basis
